oneLiner: The AI compute monopoly-in-practice: ~93% of revenue is data center growing 117% at 75% gross margins - and the balance sheet is now the strategy, with $50B+ of equity stakes in exclusive chip buyers and a $105B financing backstop for OpenAI's Ohio campus.
thesis: CUDA plus full-system integration (GPU + Vera CPU + NVLink + racks) remains the deepest lock-in in semis; the annual Hopper-Blackwell-Rubin cadence keeps rivals aiming at a moving target.
Hyperscaler capex is estimated around $725B in 2026 (vs ~$410B in 2025) with ~$1T projected for 2027; NVDA captures the largest single share of that spend.

The balance sheet has become a demand engine. NVDA's Aug 14 13F revealed a $30B Intel stake (214.8M shares, from a $5B outlay) and a $21B SpaceX stake (122.8M shares via the xAI merger conversion) - both exclusive or committed chip buyers - plus Aug 10 MOUs with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize $500B+ of AI infrastructure capital, and an up-to-$105B financing backstop (announced Aug 17) for OpenAI's 8GW Ohio data center.

Forward P/E of ~22-24x is below the trailing multiple and below the 30-40x band of 2023-2025: the market is already pricing sharp deceleration, so the debate is about duration of the capex cycle, not the multiple.
China is effectively a free option: H200 licenses exist (~$10B approved) but Beijing has blocked purchases; current numbers embed roughly zero China revenue.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 FY2027 (ended Jul 26, 2026; reported Aug 26, 2026)
points: Revenue $96.2B, +106% YoY, +18% QoQ (~$5B above the $91B guide midpoint); Data Center $89.0B, +117% YoY.
GAAP gross margin 75.0%; operating margin 66.2% (operating income $63.7B, +124% YoY).

Guide: Q3 FY2027 revenue $108.0B plus or minus 2%, gross margin 74.0% plus or minus 50bp; zero China DC compute assumed. Call: FY2028 revenue guided to ~70% growth; supply commitments doubled q/q to $279B.

segments: Data Center ~93% of revenue ($89.0B in Q2 FY27, +117% YoY): Blackwell/GB300 is the volume platform; Vera Rubin now ramping into full production with racks running at CoreWeave, Google Cloud and Azure.
Edge Computing ~7% ($7.2B in Q2 FY27, +27% YoY): Gaming, Professional Visualization, Automotive; Microsoft partnership to put 1-petaflop RTX Spark into Windows PCs.

Strategic portfolio (new): $30B Intel stake and $21B SpaceX stake disclosed Aug 14, 2026 (June 30 marks; the Intel position was ~$22B by Aug 14 after Intel's $20B offering), plus a $1.5B investment in SB Energy.
competitive: AMD MI400 series narrows the hardware gap but trails on software ecosystem.
Custom ASICs are the most credible threat: Broadcom (Google TPU, Meta MTIA, OpenAI), Marvell (Trainium, Maia) take share-of-wallet at the largest, most concentrated buyers.
Cerebras (CBRS) IPO'd May 2026 with a 750MW OpenAI deal: small revenue but a validated wafer-scale inference alternative.
Hyperscaler in-house silicon (TPU v7, Trainium 3, Maia 2) grows faster than merchant GPUs in 2026 (TrendForce: +45% vs +16%).
Equity-and-financing ties (Intel co-development, SpaceX/xAI Colossus, OpenAI Ohio) lock large buyers to NVDA silicon in ways rivals cannot match - and invite circularity critiques.
moat: CUDA and the surrounding software stack, compounded by full-system integration competitors must replicate across six-plus co-designed chips, an annual platform cadence, and a 350+-factory supply chain ramped for Rubin. Increasingly reinforced by capital: equity stakes and financing guarantees that make NVDA the anchor allocator of the AI buildout.
risks: Customer concentration: three direct customers were 21%, 17% and 16% of Q1 FY27 revenue (54% combined).

Circular financing: NVDA now backstops up to $105B for OpenAI's Ohio campus (scaled back from ~$250B discussed), holds stakes in chip-buying counterparties, and mobilizes partner capital toward its own demand - vendor-finance structures flatter revenue quality and concentrate downside if AI returns disappoint.
AI capex cycle: any hyperscaler digestion pause hits NVDA disproportionately; 2027 capex guidance this fall is the swing factor.
China effectively zero: H200 licensed but unbought; Blackwell-derivative China status unclear.
Custom silicon substitution at precisely the three concentrated customers.
Power constraints: US data center power demand projected ~66GW in 2027 vs ~31GW in 2026; Ohio's first 800MW does not arrive until 2028.
Rubin execution: first shipments Q3 2026, volume Q4 2026; slippage hits FY2028 estimates.
catalysts: Q3 FY2027 earnings ~Nov 2026 (guide $108B, GM ~74%) - first quarter with Rubin in full production.
Rubin volume ramp through Q4 2026 (racks already running at CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Azure).
OpenAI Ohio (PORTS-Pike) milestones: SB Energy buildout, financing syndication of the $105B backstop.
pricedIn: At ~$225 (mid-Aug 2026, up ~6% over the past month), implied forward EPS is roughly $9-10 (22-24x forward vs ~32x trailing). Paying a market-plus multiple for 100%+ growth means steep deceleration is already the base case - though the Aug 26 print (FY28 guided ~+70%) pushed the deceleration out a year. The new layer: the market must now underwrite NVDA as financier - a $105B Ohio guarantee, $50B+ of equity stakes marked through Intel and SpaceX share prices, and $500B of MOU capital - which bulls read as demand visibility through 2030 (~1.5M GPUs, $150-200B potential revenue per generation at Ohio alone) and bears read as the cycle funding itself. Key debates: durability of $725B-to-$1T hyperscaler capex, revenue quality given 54% three-customer concentration, and whether vendor financing pulls forward or manufactures demand.

scenarios.bear: 2027 hyperscaler capex flattens as AI ROI questions bite; custom ASICs take incremental inference share; the Ohio backstop and equity stakes turn from optionality to liability as marks fall; China stays zero; growth decelerates to teens by FY2028, gross margin slips below 70%; multiple de-rates toward high-teens on cyclical-plus-credit-risk reclassification.
scenarios.base: Rubin ramps on schedule H2 2026; hyperscaler capex grows into 2027 (~$1T); Data Center revenue +35-45% in FY2028 at ~75% gross margin; the $105B Ohio guarantee syndicates without drawing on NVDA; China negligible; stock compounds roughly with earnings at a low-20s forward multiple.
scenarios.bull: Rubin's ~5x uplift accelerates replacement cycles; agentic inference demand scales faster than training; Ohio's 1.5M-GPU pipeline plus the $500B MOU capital converts to multi-year committed demand; China unlock adds a low-double-digit revenue layer; FY2028 estimates rise materially and the multiple re-rates toward high-20s/30s.

valPresets.note: Growth presets are year-1 rates that fade to terminal: base (30% fading) roughly matches the ~18% constant growth the reverse DCF says is priced in.
